clue.text: Duck, dog and rabbit, say

parts.note: to bob is to duck down quickly
to tail someone is to dog or follow them

explanation.surface: A list of animals: a duck, a dog and a rabbit.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck and dog look like nouns in a list of animals, but both are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobtail is an animal with a short tail, and the rabbit, with its white scut, is the classic example.

clue.text: Howled aloud as commanded

indicators.note: aloud says the word for howled is to be heard when spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a hound that howled bayed

explanation.surface: Someone howled out loud just as they were told to.
explanation.definitionFit: Bade is the old past tense of bid, meaning ordered or told someone to do something.

clue.text: Ram ran to result in chaotic speculation

parts.note: a ram butts, so it is a butter, one that butts
to fly is to run away or flee; the clue uses the past tense loosely
to effect something is to bring it about, to result in it

explanation.surface: A sheep's charge leads to wild guesswork about what happens next.
explanation.walkthrough: Ram reads as a sheep or a verb meaning to strike, but it gives BUTTER, one who butts. The tense of ran against FLY is a setter's licence.
explanation.definitionFit: The idea from chaos theory that a butterfly flapping its wings might eventually cause a distant storm is a famous piece of speculation.

clue.text: A barrage gunners sent up for many vessels

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the run of pieces is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: a barrage is a dam across a river
RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners

explanation.surface: Artillery fires a barrage at a great fleet of ships.
explanation.walkthrough: Barrage suggests gunfire alongside gunners, but here it is the river-damming sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a large fleet of warships, most famously the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: Wolfish howl up in eastern passage

annotationWithheld.why: Wolfish howl up in eastern passage: LUPINE is UP inside LINE (passage), but howl and eastern then have no job, and no reading gives them letters; the clue may be misprinted.
annotationWithheld.clue: Wolfish howl up in eastern passage

clue.text: Type coming first in cut for source of cash

indicators.note: in places the type and first letter inside the word for cut

parts.note: to mow grass is to cut it
ilk means type or kind

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of coming

explanation.surface: An instruction about putting a kind of thing first in a reduction, to raise money.
explanation.walkthrough: Cut looks like a reduction in money, which suits the cash theme, but here it is the mowing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A milk cow is something that reliably yields money, like a cow giving milk; the same idea as a cash cow.

clue.text: Opiate to transform in ecstasy

parts.note: to morph is to transform smoothly from one shape to another
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drug that turns you into someone else while on a high.
explanation.definitionFit: Morphine is the principal painkilling alkaloid of opium, so it is an opiate.

clue.text: Timber roof covering Middle English court

indicators.note: covering means the roof word goes round the outside of the others

parts.note: a lid is a top or roof over a container
to court someone is to woo them

explanation.surface: Old wooden roofing over a medieval English courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: Court looks like a law court but is the verb, to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: Limewood is the wood of the lime or linden tree, prized by carvers, so it is a kind of timber.

clue.text: Haberdasher uses these precautions

definitions.meaning: a haberdasher measures out ribbon and cloth on the shop counter, so these are measures used at a counter
steps taken to counteract a threat or danger

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer into two words: the measuring done on a shop counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Countermeasures are actions taken against a danger, which is what precautions are.

clue.text: Fruit won over the Spanish after a time

indicators.note: won goes over, around, the remaining pieces
after puts the Spanish article behind a time

parts.note: a term is a period of time, as in a school term
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A fruit was won by Spain after a while.
explanation.walkthrough: Won over sounds like persuaded, but over is a container signal wrapping the word won round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A watermelon is the large juicy fruit of a trailing vine of the gourd family.

clue.text: Dirt turned over at observation base

indicators.note: over has the turned dirt go over, around, the word at
turned means the word for dirt is read backwards

parts.note: mud is wet dirt

explanation.surface: Muck flipped over at the foot of a lookout post.
explanation.walkthrough: Observation base reads as a military post, but it is the definition: a fixed fact to build on.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single observed fact or a fixed reference point from which measurements are taken.

clue.text: Normal to get a ride over everything

parts.note: par is the normal or average level
a mount is a horse to ride

explanation.surface: An ordinary person gets a lift that goes above it all.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means supreme, above all others in importance, which is being over everything.

clue.text: As Ophelia was going nowhere …

definitions.meaning: in Hamlet, Ophelia drowned in a brook, so she ended up drowned in a stream
an idiom for a plan or project that has stalled with no prospect of progress

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue on into the next one, but each clue stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalled scheme is described by the idiom as being like a boat lying motionless on the sea.

clue.text: Believe old woman getting married holds good in Wiltshire

parts.note: trow is an archaic word for believe

indicators.note: holds means the bride word has the letter for good inside it

parts.note: a bride is a woman on her wedding day

explanation.surface: An elderly woman's wedding in a West Country county is thought well of.
explanation.walkthrough: Old woman reads as a phrase, but old belongs with Believe.
explanation.definitionFit: Trowbridge is the county town of Wiltshire, so it is a place in that county.

clue.text: … right to embrace, if parting

indicators.note: to embrace means the letters for right go round the word if

parts.note: RT is an abbreviation for right, as in Rt Hon

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: it is right to hug, if you are saying goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading ellipsis links the surface to 11 across but plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rift is a split or breach between people, a parting of the ways.

clue.text: Where the bookies are often heading?

definitions.meaning: bookmakers set up at the racecourse on race days
a ship or plan heading the right way is not deviating from its intended route

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits as on course, meaning at the racecourse; the second is the idiom for keeping to plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on track toward a goal and being physically at the racecourse are both said with the same phrase.

clue.text: Representative of place where witch-hunt was trapping small one

indicators.note: trapping means the town holds the letter for small inside it

parts.note: Salem, Massachusetts, was the scene of the witch trials of 1692
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
an means one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A delegate from the town of the witch trials caught a little one.
explanation.definitionFit: A sales representative, a rep, is a salesman.

clue.text: Cassette playing sets a precedent

indicators.note: playing says the letters are moved about as a tape is played

explanation.surface: A tape being played sets the standard for others.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a tape player; playing is the anagram signal, and sets a is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A test case is a legal action whose outcome is used as a precedent for later cases.

clue.text: Traveller utterly deserted child and maiden

annotationWithheld.why: Traveller utterly deserted child and maiden: utterly suggests a homophone of WAIF (deserted child), but no sense of maiden gives the rest of WAYFARER's sound, and no source gives the parse.
annotationWithheld.clue: Traveller utterly deserted child and maiden

clue.text: The kind of tolerance that means nothing

definitions.meaning: ... tolerance is a policy of permitting no breach at all

explanation.walkthrough: That means is the link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure 0 represents no quantity at all, and the same word names a strict policing policy.

clue.text: Viking men or Dickens' characters

indicators.note: characters means letters, here a run of letters found within the words men or Dickens

explanation.surface: Norsemen, or else people from Dickens novels.
explanation.walkthrough: Dickens' characters suggests Pip or Fagin, but characters are letters in men or Dickens.
explanation.definitionFit: Nordic means Scandinavian, the region and people from which the Vikings came, so the two are used as adjectives alike.

clue.text: Promise of parking on port side

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the parking letter above the rest

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
port is the left side of a ship, giving L for left
an edge is a side or border

explanation.surface: A guarantee of somewhere to park on the left of the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Port side looks like one phrase but splits into port, L, and side, EDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge is a solemn promise or undertaking.

clue.text: Thought to take away like a vampire

parts.note: reflection is careful thought
less means minus, take away, as in arithmetic

explanation.surface: Someone thinks about stealing like a bloodsucker.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says a vampire casts no image in a mirror, so it shows no likeness of itself there.

clue.text: Stuff that's left out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of left are put out of order

explanation.surface: Something that has been omitted.
explanation.walkthrough: That's left out reads as omitted; out is the anagram signal and that's a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Felt is a fabric, and stuff is an old word for woven material or cloth.

clue.text: Nod?

parts.note: the Land of Nod is the proverbial place of sleep, so a one-word reference to the realm one drifts off into

explanation.definitionFit: The Land of Nod is a jocular name for sleep, the place where we go to dream.

clue.text: Good part of awful song

indicators.note: part of says good becomes a part inside the word for awful

parts.note: dire means awful or dreadful

explanation.surface: Some of a dreadful song is good.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song or lament, sung at a funeral.

clue.text: Understanding when temporary dwelling is in quarters

indicators.note: is in places the tent inside the compass points

parts.note: the quarters of the compass are given as letters, here E, N and E
a tent is a temporary shelter

explanation.surface: An agreement reached while a tent is pitched in the living quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: Quarters suggests lodgings, which suits a dwelling, but here it means compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly understanding between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale.

clue.text: Not a lot of space prepared for flame bearer

annotationWithheld.why: Not a lot of space prepared for flame bearer: SET is prepared, but no reading of Not a lot of space gives CRES (or CRESS with ET), so one word or more has no clear job.
annotationWithheld.clue: Not a lot of space prepared for flame bearer
